"What grows is the voltage across each, which nothing on the swing matches" is not true. How high the swing goes, far more than each push, is the counterpart of the capacitor's voltage rising past the supply, and the swing's gravity pull and inertia grow and cancel like the two part voltages. Name that match and put the break where it really is: one swinging object against two separate parts that hand energy back and forth, and shoves against a smooth supply.

Each part in a series circuit near resonance must be rated for Q times the supply, not the supply, which is Kuphaldt's "dangerously high" warning that the brief promised. That advice is only in practice.text, and a steps lesson does not show practice.text, so add one sentence to screen 7 or the finish. It is the payoff for an electrician.

The screen says X_L points up and X_C down but not why: the coil's voltage peaks a quarter cycle before the current and the capacitor's a quarter cycle after, so they are half a cycle apart. A steps lesson does not show the explain text, so on screen this cause first appears in screen 8. Add the one clause before screen 2 asks for the net.
